title: Cursor vs GitHub Copilot vs Windsurf (2026): Which AI Code Editor Should You Use?
description: 60 days using all three AI-native IDEs daily. Coding speed, multi-file edits, agent quality, pricing — which one wins for solo devs vs teams in 2026?
short_desc: The 3-way coding assistant comparison. SWE-Bench tested.
tldr_pick: Cursor for the best AI-native IDE experience. GitHub Copilot for the safest enterprise default. Windsurf if you want Cursor-class features at $5/mo less.
key_takeaways: Cursor leads on AI-native IDE polish and multi-file editing
GitHub Copilot has the deepest IDE integration (every editor, every platform)
Windsurf is 75% of Cursor at $15/mo instead of $20/mo
All three pass ~70%+ on SWE-Bench Verified with Claude Sonnet

faq.q: Which is best for solo developers?
faq.a: Cursor. The multi-file editing UX (Composer) is unmatched and worth $20/mo for serious daily coding.
GitHub Copilot. It integrates with GitHub Enterprise, has admin controls, and works in every editor your team already uses.
Yes — Windsurf is now genuinely competitive with Cursor since the Cognition acquisition. Save $5/mo if you don't need Cursor's specific UI polish.

verdict_headline: Cursor is the best for solo devs, Copilot for teams, Windsurf for budget
verdict_body: All three are excellent. Pick based on your workflow, not benchmark scores.
methodology: We used all three daily for 60 days across Python, TypeScript, and Rust projects. We measured completion quality, multi-file coherence, agent mode reliability, and pricing changes. All three services were paid out-of-pocket.
